original_question: Can one find a Hardy-field function a(t) with super-polynomial growth, meaning a(t)/t^k → ∞ for every k, such that the integer sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.5, Problem 26 ("Hardy sequences of super-polynomial growth").
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely: it asks for existence of a Hardy-field function a(t), imposes the correct super-polynomial growth condition a(t)/t^k -> infinity for every k, uses the integer-part sequence [a(n)], and asks for exactly the two properties singled out in the paper, namely multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers.
missing_details: The paper formulates this as an existence problem for a function a in H, where H is the union of all Hardy fields of germs of real-valued functions defined on some half-line (c, infinity), not just an informal 'Hardy-field function.'
It should specify that [a(n)] means the integer part of a(n).

The phrase 'of powers' refers to powers of a single invertible measure-preserving transformation T; this should be made explicit so the question is not confused with the separate commuting-transformations problems.

The recurrence part should be unpacked: for every ell in N and every integers k1,...,kell, every invertible measure-preserving system (X, B, mu, T), and every A in B with mu(A) > 0, there exists n in N such that mu(A ∩ T^{-k1[a(n)]}A ∩ ... ∩ T^{-kell[a(n)]}A) > 0.

The convergence part should be unpacked: for every ell in N, integers k1,...,kell, every invertible measure-preserving system (X, B, mu, T), and every f1,...,fell in L^infinity(mu), the averages (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N T^{k1[a(n)]}f1 ... T^{kell[a(n)]}fell converge in the mean (i.e. in L^2(mu)).
The growth condition should be stated as a limit as t -> infinity.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should ask to 'find an example' (or equivalently ask for existence), not to characterize all such functions.
refined_question: Does there exist a function a in H, where H denotes the union of all Hardy fields of real-valued germs on some half-line (c, infinity), such that a(t)/t^k -> infinity as t -> infinity for every k in N and the integer-part sequence ([a(n)])_{n in N} is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation; that is, for every ell in N and every integers k1,...,kell, every invertible measure-preserving system (X, B, mu, T), every A in B with mu(A) > 0, and every f1,...,fell in L^infinity(mu), one has both: (i) there exists n in N with mu(A ∩ T^{-k1[a(n)]}A ∩ ... ∩ T^{-kell[a(n)]}A) > 0, and (ii) the averages (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N T^{k1[a(n)]}f1 ... T^{kell[a(n)]}fell converge in L^2(mu)?
justification: This is essentially a sharpening of the exact open problem stated in Section 6.1.5, Problem 26. The nearby setup in Section 6 defines H and 'Hardy sequence' as ([a(n)]), while Definitions 3.2 and 3.4 give the precise meanings of 'good for multiple recurrence of powers' and 'good for multiple convergence of powers.' The surrounding context also shows that the problem is specifically about powers of a single transformation, and that the polynomial-growth case is already understood, so the open problem is to exhibit one super-polynomial Hardy example rather than to broaden the question further.
